title: Singapore Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon to Step Down in February 2027, Sushil Nair Named Successor
excerpt: The Indian-origin jurist, who transformed Singapore's legal landscape over 14 years, will be succeeded by fellow Indian-origin judge Sushil Nair in what the Prime Minister's Office called a planned transition.
body:
• Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon will retire by February 27, 2027, a day after his 65th birthday, ending a 14-year tenure that reshaped Singapore's judiciary.
  • Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair, also of Indian origin, has been named as the fifth Chief Justice of Singapore, continuing an extraordinary representation of the Indian diaspora at the highest levels of Singapore's legal system.
  • Menon was the first Singapore-born Chief Justice and pioneered major reforms in legal technology, professional ethics, and the establishment of the Singapore International Commercial Court.
  • Nair brings 35 years of legal experience from Drew & Napier, specializing in restructuring across the Asia-Pacific region, and was rapidly elevated through three judicial appointments in under two years.

A Historic Tenure Draws to a Close

Singapore's Prime Minister's Office announced on July 17 that Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon will retire from the bench by February 27, 2027 — one day after he turns 65, the constitutional retirement age for Singapore's judiciary. The announcement also confirmed that Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair will succeed him as the fifth Chief Justice of the Republic.

Menon's departure marks the end of an era that began in November 2012, when he became Singapore's fourth Chief Justice and its first born in the city-state. An Indian-origin jurist educated at the National University of Singapore and Harvard Law School, Menon rose through the ranks from founding partner at WongPartnership to Attorney-General before his appointment to the Supreme Court bench.

"I am greatly honoured and privileged to be entrusted with this awesome responsibility; and humbled by the calibre of those who have been so entrusted before me."

— Sundaresh Menon, upon his appointment as Chief Justice in 2012

"Appointed Judicial Commissioner in April 2025, he was elevated to High Court Judge in March 2026 and then to Justice of the Court of Appeal just three months later in June 2026."

A Legacy of Institutional Reform

Under Menon's leadership, Singapore's judiciary underwent a quiet transformation. He oversaw the establishment of the Singapore International Commercial Court in 2015, designed to attract cross-border commercial disputes and cement Singapore's position as a global dispute resolution hub. The court now includes 26 international judges drawn from leading jurisdictions worldwide.

Menon also drove reforms in legal education and professional ethics, commissioning a comprehensive review that resulted in tighter conduct standards, investment restrictions for judicial officers, and new pathways for continuing legal education. His speeches on transnational justice and legal pluralism have been widely cited in academic literature across Asia.

Beyond the courtroom, Menon served as President of the ASEAN Law Association from 2018 to 2023, strengthening judicial cooperation frameworks across Southeast Asia. Under his watch, the association produced guidelines on cross-border arbitral award enforcement and launched youth development programs for lawyers across the region.

Nair's Rapid Rise to the Top

His successor, Sushil Sukumaran Nair, has had one of the fastest ascents in Singapore's judicial history. Appointed Judicial Commissioner in April 2025, he was elevated to High Court Judge in March 2026 and then to Justice of the Court of Appeal just three months later in June 2026. His appointment as Chief Justice-designate caps a meteoric rise from the private sector.

Nair spent 35 years at Drew & Napier, one of Singapore's most prestigious law firms, where he served as Deputy Chief Executive Officer and headed the corporate restructuring practice. He earned recognition as a Band 1 restructuring lawyer by Chambers Asia Pacific for 17 consecutive years. Beyond commercial law, he played a public service role — he received Singapore's Public Service Star for drafting the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Bill in 2020, legislation that proved integral to the country's pandemic response.

What It Means for the Indian Diaspora

The succession from one Indian-origin Chief Justice to another underscores the remarkable standing of the Indian community in Singapore's public institutions. Ethnic Indians make up roughly 7.4 percent of Singapore's population, yet have held the country's highest judicial office continuously since 2012.

For the broader diaspora, Menon's tenure represents the kind of institutional leadership that extends beyond corporate achievement. His work in building judicial cooperation frameworks across ASEAN has implications for cross-border commerce and dispute resolution that directly affect Indian businesses operating in Southeast Asia.

Looking Ahead

Nair is expected to formally assume the role on February 27, 2027. The transition comes as Singapore prepares to celebrate the bicentennial of its modern legal system — the 200th anniversary of the Second Charter of Justice — a milestone Menon himself highlighted in his final Legal Year address in January 2026. He will leave behind a Supreme Court bench of 33 judges and 26 international judges, the largest and most internationally diverse in the court's history.
